**1. `internal/cli/git_catfile_batch.go:79-110` — the git spawn preamble is copy-pasted from the runner, creating a second git spawn point.**
Lines 83-96 replicate `runExecCommand` (`internal/cli/runner.go:85-104`) and `ExecRunner.Stream` (`runner.go:147-164`) verbatim: `hardenedGitArgs(...)` → `repoFilterDriverOverrides(ctx, dir)` → `gitConfigOverrideEnv(mergeCommandEnv(os.Environ(), env), overrides)`. `hardenedGitArgs`'s own doc comment (`internal/cli/git_harden.go:189-192`) claims it is unbypassable precisely because "it is applied at the single point where this binary actually spawns git (see runner.go)" — this file makes that comment false. Use instead: extract the shared preamble out of `runner.go` (or add a stdin-capable variant alongside `ExecRunner.Stream`) and have the batch child go through it, so hardening/filter-override policy stays in one place.

**2. `internal/cli/git_catfile_batch.go:94-108` — the hand-rolled child drops two safeguards the runner path already provides.**
No `cmd.WaitDelay = commandWaitDelay` (`runner.go:73`, deliberately set on both existing spawn paths) and no stderr capture, where `cappedBuffer` (`runner.go:198`) is the existing bounded-stderr writer used by `ExecRunner.Stream`; the child's stderr is silently discarded, so a broken child produces only "read header: EOF". Use instead: `cappedBuffer{limit: streamStderrCap}` and `commandWaitDelay` from `runner.go`.

**3. `internal/cli/git_catfile_batch.go:35,175-182` — the size guard reinvents the repo's read-bound helper and its error type.**
`catFileBatchMaxBlobBytes` plus the `fmt.Errorf("... is %d bytes, over the %d byte guard")` duplicates `readBoundExceededError` (`internal/cli/safe_read.go:154-161`, message "%s exceeds maximum size of %d bytes") and the `safeReadAll(r, max, source)` bound (`safe_read.go:163`). Because it returns a plain error, the existing size-aware callers that classify oversized reads via `errors.As(&readBoundExceededError{})` — `internal/cli/conversation.go:692` and `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:401`, both reachable from `catFileWithPolicy` results — will no longer recognize this as a size failure. Use instead: `&readBoundExceededError{source: spec, max: catFileBatchMaxBlobBytes}`, and `safeReadAll` over an `io.LimitReader` of the record body.

**4. `internal/cli/git_catfile_batch.go:65-71` — `commandRunnerIsExec` uses a concrete-type switch where the package's established seam is an optional capability interface.**
The codebase detects runner capabilities by interface assertion, never by concrete type: `EnvironmentCommandRunner` (`runner.go:26`, asserted at `export.go:693`) and `CommandStreamer` (`runner.go:36`, asserted at `semantic_stream.go:455`, `brain_brief_git_intent.go:145`, `brain_brief_stale_index.go:306`). The new type switch also silently skips the fast path for any wrapper around `ExecRunner`. Use instead: declare the batch capability as an optional interface in `runner.go` alongside `CommandStreamer` and assert it the same way.

**5. `internal/cli/git_catfile_batch_test.go:13-35` — `newBatchTestRepo` re-implements an existing temp-repo fixture and its git runner.**
The inner `run` closure (env-neutralized `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` + pinned author/committer, `CombinedOutput`, `t.Fatalf("git %v: %v\n%s", ...)`) is line-for-line `liveGit` at `internal/cli/entities_live_e2e_test.go:52-76` — which carries a long comment explaining exactly why those env vars are needed. The "temp dir + init + one committed file" fixture already exists as `gitHardenRepo` (`internal/cli/git_harden_security_test.go:65`, with `gitHardenRun` at :53 and the `--template=` hardening these tests also want), and `gitAt` (`internal/cli/degenerate_repo_test.go:20`) is the package-scoped generic git-in-a-dir helper. Use instead: `liveGit` for the git invocations (or promote `gitHardenRun`/`gitAt` to a shared fixture); note the new code also hardcodes `"/dev/null"` where every other call site uses `os.DevNull`.
